title: The Problem of Induction and Scientific Justification
text:
Induction concerns the process of inferring general rules or theories from a set of specific observations. A central challenge to this method is the problem of induction, which highlights that past successful outcomes do not logically guarantee future ones. The core assumption—that nature operates according to consistent laws and that observed instances predict unobserved ones—is fundamentally unfalsifiable by pure logic.

The philosophical skepticism surrounding induction was notably articulated by David Hume. He argued that while inductive reasoning is essential for daily scientific inquiry and predictive modeling, its justification rests not on logical necessity, but rather on custom or habit. This realization prompts a debate regarding the ultimate epistemic limits of empirical knowledge.
